title: Chapter 5 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of ARIA roles, states, properties, and widget patterns.

questions.question: What does ARIA stand for?
questions.explanation: ARIA = Accessible Rich Internet Applications, a W3C spec.

questions.question: What is the first rule of ARIA?
options: Do not use ARIA if native HTML can do the job
ARIA is only for screen readers
questions.explanation: Native elements provide built‑in semantics and behaviour; ARIA should supplement, not replace.

questions.question: Adding `role="button"` to a `<div>` automatically makes it respond to the Enter key.
questions.explanation: ARIA adds no behaviour. You must add JavaScript for keyboard and click handling.

questions.question: To make a non‑focusable element reachable via Tab, you set `tabindex="__"`.
questions.explanation: `tabindex="0"` inserts the element into the natural tab order.

questions.question: Which attribute provides an accessible name when no visible text label exists?
questions.explanation: `aria-label` allows direct string input for the name. `aria-labelledby` references visible text.

questions.question: What role do you assign to the container of individual tabs?
questions.explanation: The parent wrapper gets `role="tablist"`.

questions.question: `aria-selected` should be used on accordion headers to indicate the open panel.
questions.explanation: Accordions use `aria-expanded` to convey open/closed state; `aria-selected` is for selectable items like tabs or list options.

questions.question: What does `aria-hidden="true"` do?
options: Removes the element from the DOM
Makes the element invisible to assistive technologies
questions.explanation: It hides the element from the accessibility tree, but it remains visible on screen.

questions.question: Which keyboard interaction is expected for a set of tabs?
options: Tab to move between tabs; Enter to open panel
Arrow keys to move between tabs; Tab to enter the active panel
questions.explanation: Left/Right arrows switch tabs; Tab moves focus into the currently visible tab panel.

questions.question: What attribute indicates that a dialog is modal and content outside should be ignored?
questions.explanation: `aria-modal="true"` informs assistive tech that only the dialog content is relevant.

questions.question: What should happen when a modal dialog is closed?
options: Focus should be removed from the page
Focus should return to the element that triggered the dialog
The next focusable element on the page should be focused
questions.explanation: Restoring focus to the trigger preserves user context.

questions.question: Which live region value announces updates without interrupting the user?
questions.explanation: `aria-live="polite"` waits until the screen reader is idle before speaking.

questions.question: `role="alert"` implies `aria-live="assertive"` and `aria-atomic="true"`.
questions.explanation: An alert role is an assertive live region that reads the entire content when it changes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `aria-describedby`?
options: To link an element to additional description text
questions.explanation: It adds supplementary information, like error messages or hints, to the element's announcement.

questions.question: You have two `<nav>` elements on a page. How do you differentiate them for screen readers?
options: Use one `<nav>` and CSS to style them differently
No need, screen readers ignore duplicates
questions.explanation: `aria-label='Main navigation'` and `aria-label='Footer navigation'` make the landmarks distinguishable.

questions.question: Which attribute must you update via JavaScript when an accordion panel opens?
questions.explanation: `aria-expanded` toggles between true/false as the panel shows/hides.

questions.question: You can safely apply `aria-hidden="true"` to a focusable element because it will be skipped in the tab order.
questions.explanation: Focusable elements with `aria-hidden="true"` create a confusing experience: focus is visible but the screen reader stays silent.

questions.question: Which native HTML element is now preferred for creating modal dialogs?
questions.explanation: The `<dialog>` element provides built‑in modal behaviour, focus trapping, and backdrop styling.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `aria-controls` in a tab pattern?
options: To indicate which panel a tab controls
questions.explanation: `aria-controls` points to the ID of the controlled element, helping assistive tech understand relationships.

questions.question: Why might a live region not announce repeated identical text?
options: Screen readers may ignore duplicate strings
questions.explanation: To force re‑announcement, clear the region and reinsert the text after a short delay.

questions.question: Which attribute takes precedence in naming: `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`?
questions.explanation: `aria-labelledby` has higher priority than `aria-label` in the accessible name computation.

questions.question: The `inert` attribute can be used to make all content outside a dialog unfocusable and invisible to assistive tech.
questions.explanation: `inert` removes the element and its children from the tab order and accessibility tree.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid ARIA state that changes over time?
questions.explanation: States like `aria-expanded` reflect current condition; properties like `aria-label` are static.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of the native `<dialog>` element over a custom ARIA dialog?
options: It provides built‑in focus trapping, backdrop, and keyboard handling
questions.explanation: `<dialog>` handles focus management, escape key, and backdrop automatically, reducing custom JS.
